odd: If something is odd, it is not normal and usually you don't like it or don't understand it.
The neighbours thought him very odd, because he would leave his doors open all night.
The odd time, drink, problem, etc. is one that happens sometimes, but not often.
I don't really drink – just the odd beer at the weekend.
An odd sock, boot, etc. is one without its pair.
The clown was wearing odd socks.
An odd number is one that does not divide evenly by 2 (e.g., 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, etc.)
A count of (number)-odd is just a little more than the number.
I've got fifty-odd students in the class.
odyssey: A long adventurous journey or trip.
The odyssey of Odysseus was written down by Homer in his epic poem, the Odyssey.
An intellectual or spiritual journey or quest.
oddity: That's quite an oddity you have there. I think people would pay to see something that rare.
odds: , In statistics, the odds are the chance something will happen divided by the chance it will not happen:
What are the odds of winning in this game?
, The odds of something happening are the chances it will happen.
I don't like the odds here.
odorless: If something is odorless, it does not have an odor.
odourless: If something is odourless, it does not have an odor.
odor: Something's odor is its smell, usually a bad smell.
The football players had an odor after their match, and I had to hold my breath as they walked past.
odour: Something's odour is its smell, usually a bad smell.
The football players had an odour after their match, and I had to hold my breath as they walked past.
odometer: An odometer is an instrument that measures the distance a vehicle traveled.
odysseus: Odysseus is a Greek king of Ithaca, responsible for the Trojan horse, and is the hero of the Odyssey.
oddly: To do something oddly is to do it in an odd manner.
oddness: The oddness of someone is how odd they are.
odorous: If something is odorous, it has a distinctive odor.
odoriferous: If something is odoriferous, it has a distinctive odor.
